question: Which SI base unit is directly derived from the definition of ampere?
solution:
The correct answer is __Coulomb**(C)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Coulomb__ is the SI unit of electric charge.
 
• It is derived directly from the definition of ampere, which is the SI unit of electric current.
 
• One coulomb is defined as the amount of charge transferred by a current of one ampere in one second.
 
• The relationship between ampere and coulomb is expressed as 1 C = 1 A × 1 s.
 
• The coulomb is named after Charles-Augustin de Coulomb, a French physicist.
 
• This unit is fundamental in understanding electric charge and current flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Watt:**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of power and is derived from the base units kilogram, meter, and second.
 
• It is equal to one joule per second.
 
 
 
• **Volt:**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of electric potential and is derived from the base units kilogram, meter, second, and ampere.
 
• It is defined as the potential difference across a conductor when one ampere of current dissipates one watt of power.
 
 
 
• **Ohm:**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of electrical resistance and is derived from the base units kilogram, meter, second, and ampere.
 
• One ohm is equal to one volt per ampere.
